title: PatchPad Editor 1.3 - QC Rework
subtitle: Closure review against PatchPad_Editor_QC.xlsx
note: All 13 prior findings were rechecked. Static, local restart, and Docker golden checks completed on 2026-08-25; a fresh Harbor Oracle run remains the final release gate.

runs.note: Superseded evidence: the prior batched judge relied on compacted-session summaries for seven criteria.
Superseded score: the QC found multiple unsupported passes. The new evidence gate rejects the archived run's missing-marker reasoning.

tasks.name: PatchPad 1.3
tasks.headline: 13 of 13 prior findings are structurally closed; run a fresh Oracle before release to replace the superseded 1.2 proof.

findings.what: The prior batched judge awarded criteria without performing their exact named probes.
findings.why: Unsupported awards made the reported model score non-reproducible.
findings.impact: Incorrect positive training signal and an inflated model score.
findings.fix: Changed the agent judge to individual per-criterion calls and recompute reward after a marker-based evidence gate rejects incomplete or prior-session reasoning.
findings.action: Confirm the next model run records zero evidence-gate false passes.

findings.what: The prior Oracle used compacted context summaries for 7 of 20 criteria.
findings.why: A batched 20-criterion agent call exceeded practical context and did not prove the golden end to end.
findings.impact: The old Oracle 1.0 is superseded as release evidence.
findings.fix: Each criterion now runs in its own sequential Claude Code call; prior-session wording also fails the evidence gate.
findings.action: Run a fresh Oracle and require full score with no prior-session language.

findings.what: Contiguous typing, typed selection replacement, Replace All atomicity, and redo invalidation were graded but absent from the brief.
findings.why: The rubric encoded golden-specific undo behavior the model was not told to implement.
findings.impact: A compliant submission could lose 4.0 weight for unstated behavior.
findings.fix: The Editing brief now states all four undo units in one concise paragraph.

findings.what: The prior judge repaired content after a destructive API probe and still passed the criterion.
findings.why: Repaired state is manufactured evidence rather than observed app behavior.
findings.impact: The API rejection award and all later shared-state checks were untrustworthy.
findings.fix: The API matrix is now last, mutation is an immediate failure, repair is forbidden, and repair language is rejected by the evidence gate.

findings.what: The prior run retained only free-text criterion reasoning and no Claude/Playwright transcript.
findings.why: Exact mouse and keyboard claims could not be independently audited.
findings.impact: Disputed awards had no inspectable tool-call trail.
findings.fix: New Claude Code JSONL sessions created during RewardKit are copied under rewardkit-browser/judge-transcripts with an index.
findings.action: Verify the next Harbor artifact contains non-empty transcript JSONL files.

findings.what: The pristine revision-1 seed check was not guaranteed to run before mutating criteria.
findings.why: The old batched judge evaluated it after a save and passed by inference.
findings.impact: The baseline for all later checks was unknown.
findings.fix: Individual mode evaluates the exact seed/custom-surface criterion first; a deterministic preflight independently checks manifest, non-empty SQLite, and unchanged logical DB state after restart.

findings.what: The brief allowed Alt+Click or Ctrl/Cmd+Click while both criteria required Alt only.
findings.why: A Ctrl/Cmd-only compliant editor would lose both multi-caret checks.
findings.impact: 2.0 weight could be denied for a permitted implementation choice.
findings.fix: Both criteria now accept either real modifier-click path, require one path to be chosen cleanly, and require that path to be used consistently.

findings.what: A Windows launcher exposed a private relative Node toolchain path in shipped artifacts.
findings.why: It had no Linux-container function and leaked authoring-machine structure.
findings.impact: Visible packaging noise in the client artifact.
findings.fix: Deleted run-local.cmd from the solution app.

findings.what: Restart idempotency and APP_MANIFEST completeness were mandatory but ungraded.
findings.why: A reseeding app or incomplete manifest could score like a correct submission.
findings.impact: Two explicit delivery requirements had no training pressure.
findings.fix: A 0.5-weight deterministic preflight validates the start block, SQLite path, API route listing, non-empty database, and identical logical database digest and row counts after restart.

findings.what: Unweighted passed/total counts appeared beside a weighted score without being named as criterion counts.
findings.why: Readers could not reconcile 16/20 with the 13/19 weighted reward.
findings.fix: Metrics are explicitly named browser_criteria_passed/total and separately report browser_passed_weight/total_weight.

findings.what: A stale process could theoretically occupy PORT and satisfy health checks after the intended app failed to bind.
findings.why: The old harness did not establish process ownership of the graded port.
findings.impact: No prior run was affected, but a future run could grade the wrong process.
findings.fix: The harness clears PORT with fuser before each start and fails health checks if the launched process exits.

findings.what: The prior agent used about ten minutes of a three-hour allowance.
findings.why: This was informational and did not affect correctness.
findings.fix: No change required; the difficult browser verifier, not agent wall time, defines task depth.

findings.what: The prior report recorded reward-on-crash, secret hygiene, deterministic seed arithmetic, and tiered weights as strengths.
findings.why: These controls needed to survive the rework.
findings.impact: Preserving them avoids regressions while closing the blockers.
findings.fix: All four strengths remain; crash guards and weight arithmetic were revalidated after the new preflight was added.

blocks.title: P0/P1 closure
items: Per-criterion individual judging replaces the compacted 20-check session.
The score is recomputed after an exact-marker evidence gate, so unsupported yes verdicts no longer reach reward.json.
Undo granularity is now stated in the brief, both modifier-click choices are accepted, and probe repair is forbidden.

blocks.title: Golden checks
items: The environment image builds with /instructions and /assets readable.
The golden solution starts in Docker at revision 1 with one document, one revision, and exactly 1,226 expected lines.
The deterministic preflight passes locally with identical logical SQLite digests across restart.

blocks.title: Release gate
items: Run a fresh Oracle because the previous 1.0 used the superseded batched judge.
Check that rewardkit-browser/judge-transcripts/index.json lists non-empty JSONL session files.
